questions: Can Takahashi perform a front kick in a direction that would target cells outside the grid boundaries, and if so, are those out-of-bound cells considered walls that get converted to roads?

If Takahashi performs a front kick in a direction where there are fewer than two cells ahead of his current position, does he still convert all wall cells within the available range (0 or 1 steps) in that direction?
Is it allowed for Takahashi to move into a cell that was originally a wall but has been converted to a road during the same sequence of actions, or must he wait until the next turn?
Does the problem require the minimum number of front kicks across all possible paths from start to destination, or just any valid path that reaches the destination?
Are diagonal movements allowed, or strictly only up, down, left, and right movements between adjacent cells?
If multiple front kicks are performed in the same direction from the same cell, do the effects stack (i.e., does converting a wall to a road and then kicking again have any additional effect)?
Can Takahashi choose to perform a front kick even if there are no walls within the targeted cells (i.e., are unnecessary kicks permitted)?
Is the output required to be the exact number of front kicks used, or can it include additional information such as the sequence of moves and kicks?
answers: Yes. The front kick can be performed even if the affected area partially extends outside the grid. Only the cells inside the grid are checked and changed; cells outside are ignored.
A front kick affects the two cells directly ahead; if fewer cells exist in that direction, only those existing cells are affected.
Takahashi can immediately move into a cell that was just converted to a road.
Find the minimum number of front kicks across all possible paths.
Only up, down, left, and right movements are allowed; no diagonal movements.
A cell, once converted to road, stays a road; additional kicks have no further effect.
Yes. Unnecessary kicks are permitted but increase the cost.
Output only the minimum number of front kicks, regardless of how many different paths achieve it. No path reconstruction is required.
inline_prompts:
Takahashi is about to go buy eel at a fish shop.
The town where he lives is divided into a grid of H rows and W columns. Each cell is either a road or a wall.
Let us denote the cell at the i-th row from the top (1\leq i \leq H) and the j-th column from the left (1\leq j \leq W) as cell (i,j).
Information about each cell is given by H strings S_1,S_2,\ldots,S_H, each of length W. Specifically, if the j-th character of S_i (1\leq i \leq H,1\leq j\leq W) is ., cell (i,j) is a road; if it is #, cell (i,j) is a wall.
He can repeatedly perform the following two types of actions in any order:
- Move to an adjacent cell (up, down, left, or right) that is within the town and is a road.
- Choose one of the four directions (up, down, left, or right) and perform a front kick in that direction.
When he performs a front kick, for each of the cells at most 2 steps away in that direction from the cell he is currently in, if that cell is a wall, it becomes a road. Yes. The front kick can be performed even if the affected area partially extends outside the grid. Only the cells inside the grid are checked and changed; cells outside are ignored.
He starts in cell (A,B), and he wants to move to the fish shop in cell (C,D).
It is guaranteed that both the cell where he starts and the cell with the fish shop are roads.
Find the number of front kicks he needs in order to reach the fish shop.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
S_1
S_2
\vdots
S_H
A B C D
Output
Print the number of front kicks needed for Takahashi to reach the fish shop.
Constraints
- 1\leq H\leq 1000
- 1\leq W\leq 1000
- Each S_i is a string of length W consisting of . and #.
- 1\leq A,C\leq H
- 1\leq B,D\leq W
- (A,B)\neq (C,D)
- H, W, A, B, C, and D are integers.
- The cell where Takahashi starts and the cell with the fish shop are roads.
